title: Classical Limit: Dissipation of Spekkens' Generalised Contextuality under Decoherence
summary: When does a decohering quantum system become classical? Generalised noncontextuality gives one criterion, for scenarios rich enough in preparations: a system is classical once its statistics admit an underlying model in which operationally indistinguishable procedures are physically identical. Where it crosses depends not on the state and channel alone but on which preparations, transformations and measurements the experiment offers, and if every measurement is allowed there is no crossing.
